issues.description: The template's commented example usage in Main.java shows two-argument constructors for Seal, Pig, and Goat (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), whereas the problem UML and the intended solution define constructors that only initialize the animal's name (single-argument constructors). This mismatch can confuse students about the required constructor signatures and whether additional attributes beyond 'name' must be implemented.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's example usage consistent with the specification: update the commented Main.java examples to use single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")), or alternatively update the problem statement and UML to explicitly require and document the additional constructor parameter(s) and corresponding attributes so all artifacts agree.

issues.description: The template's Main.java shows example constructors for Seal, Pig, and Goat using two parameters (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")) while the problem UML and the reference solution define these animal constructors with a single parameter (name only). This mismatch between the template example and the intended class signatures (and UML) can confuse students about the required constructor signature and which attributes to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template example with the UML and solution by changing the commented example constructors in template Main.java to single-argument forms: Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky"). Alternatively, if two-argument constructors are intended, update the UML/problem statement and solution classes to include and document the additional attribute.
